name: Belarus
summary: Belarus is under extensive EU, US and UK sanctions, which in practice rule it out for a family holding a global portfolio. From 2026 (Law No. 127-Z of 30 December 2025) employment-type income is taxed at 13% up to BYN 350,000, 25% to BYN 600,000 and 30% above, and Belarusian dividends at 13% up to BYN 350,000 and 25% above. Capital gains (securities, company shares, real estate) and foreign dividends stay at the basic 13%, with no holding-period exemption for securities. No net wealth tax and no inheritance or gift tax; inheritances and gifts from close relatives are exempt from income tax. Tax rules read from the Tax Code; no professional cross-check available.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.eligibility: Residence test (183 days in a calendar year, as generally reported) not verified. Foreigners need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on securities (Belarusian or foreign), shares in companies and real estate are taxed at the basic 13% personal income tax rate (Tax Code Art. 214(1.1)), on proceeds minus documented costs (Art. 202 for securities; property deduction Art. 211). The 25%/30% rates introduced for 2026 apply only to a listed basket of Belarus-source employment-type income and to Belarusian dividends (Art. 199(82)–(83)), not to capital gains. There is no holding-period exemption for securities or company shares. Residents may sell one dwelling, one plot, one garage etc. of each type tax-free once every five years (Art. 208(44)).

capital_gains.rate_basis: 13% basic PIT rate (Art. 214(1.1)) on net gains; the 25%/30% bands do not include capital gains (Art. 199(82)). Real estate 13% assumes more than one sale of that property type in five years; a single sale is exempt.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Once per five years per property type: one house, one flat, one plot, one dacha, one garage (Art. 208(44)); gains on Belarusian government and certain bank bonds exempt. No exemption for shares or other securities.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None for securities. Real estate: one sale per property type per five years exempt regardless of holding period.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed at 13%; Belarusian dividends above BYN 350,000 a year are taxed at 25% on the excess from 2026 (Tax Code Art. 214(1.2), base defined in Art. 199(83) as Belarus-source dividends). Foreign dividends stay at the basic 13% rate. 0% applies to Belarusian dividends where the company distributed no profit for the five preceding years (Art. 214(6)).

wealth_tax.summary: Belarus has no net wealth tax: the Tax Code's Special Part contains no such tax (its taxes on property are the real estate tax, land tax and transport tax). From 2026 the real estate tax uses multipliers for large homes (houses over 200/300 m² x2/x3; apartments over 150/250 m² x2/x3).

inheritance.summary: There is no inheritance or gift tax in the Belarusian Tax Code. Inheritances received from individuals are exempt from personal income tax (Art. 208(21)), except royalties paid to heirs of authors. Gifts from close relatives (including parent to child) are exempt (Art. 208(22¹)); a 10% charge on such gifts above 100 base units applies only to recipients registered as able-bodied persons not employed in the economy, which does not concern a family office. Gifts from non-relatives are taxable income at 13% above small allowances.

Cost of living: no international school fee for Minsk; QSI International School of Minsk does not publish fees and the only third-party figure (doris.school, USD 23,000, undated, AI-compiled) was not reliable enough to use. Health insurance, housekeeper and price per m2 not sourced.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median asking rent of 48 distinct long-term listings (interquartile range USD 1,407-2,556) of flats with 4+ rooms and at least 120 m2 in the city of Minsk on realt.by, snapshot 2026-10-15: all 1,461 long-term flat listings on the site were read and filtered; duplicates (same rooms, area, address) removed. Listings priced in BYN or EUR were converted at the National Bank of Belarus rates of 15 October 2026 (USD 1 = BYN 3.0113; EUR 1 = BYN 3.3706); the median is about BYN 5,700. Asking rents; Belarusian room counts include the living room. Large houses near Minsk (Drozdy, Ratomka, Tarasovo) list from about USD 2,500 to 7,000 but that sample is mixed with short-stay and corporate lets and was not used. Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

source.title: Realt.by - Аренда квартир на длительный срок (Минск)

cost_of_living.notes: Rent from realt.by listings.
